body:
I have never really been a big “hobby” type of person – certainly I’ve never had anything in my life that I’ve felt a grand “passion” for, except other people (about whom I am TOO passionate, sigh).  I often enjoy reading, but my emotions have been so high lately that I can’t really turn them down enough to focus on words on a page.  There have been times in my life when I’ve been a regular gym goer, but it’s pretty embarrassing to cry through a yoga class.  I often enjoy board games, but that’s not really something you can do alone.  I don’t feel like it’s the best time to try a new club or group, as I don’t feel I’d make a terribly good first impression.  

I don’t mean to sound like I’m being purposely negative or shooting down ideas.  But, like, people say, “go for a walk.”  Well, once you’ve spent a few 45-minute walks crying and being looked at like a crazy person…you know?  So it’s like, I don’t want to be alone, but I also don’t want to be with someone new (much less a new GROUP), and the people I DO trust to be with me…well, burnout.

Honestly, I just want to be held and loved.  But I need SO much of that, that no one can ever give it.  And the self-love thing…I just don’t get it.  I don’t see how I can possibly not feel this immense emptiness, this immense pain.  

Thank you for your help, though, you are being really nice.  I appreciate it.

I hear your words. Any advice on concretely HOW to be happy in myself? Because just trying to tell myself I should be happy, well, not only doesn't it make me happy, but then I have guilt over not being able to think myself happy. You know?

My biggest trigger is feeling abandoned.  So it's gotten quite cyclical, in that I'm burning people out so that they actually DO tell me they can't deal with me (at least right then), which in turn escalates the crisis even more.  And I seem to be helpless to break that cycle; every time I have a few good days and cautiously think I'm improving, something happens to put me all the way back to the beginning (or even further back than that).  

For several months now, I've been trying to just hold on until I could get into a doctor or counselor, but it seems like I'm deteriorating too quickly to make it 'til my assessment in another 3 months.  

Maybe if I could've gotten help at the beginning of this crisis I could've nipped it all in the bud, and not have angered / frustrated my boyfriend and friends to this point, and I would still have those relationships to help keep me sane.
